claims.summary: Over F2, m>n>=1 and independent original A:m by n,B:n by m, E=AB,W=prod_a!=b(1+Eab),P=W prod_a Eaa. For i<j define Di=prod_a<i Eaa,Wij=W's syntactic product omitting (1+Eij),Cij=det E_rows(i+1..m),cols(i..m except j),Kij=sum_l(B_lj Z_Ail+A_il² Z_Blj). Then Q=sum_i<j Di Wij Cij Kij is linear in every original Boolean placeholder and Q(X,b)=P,Q(X,0)=0. Nonidentity permutations grouped by their first moved row give detE+prod Eaa=sum Di Eij Cij; rank makes detE and minors of order>n zero formally, so terms i<m-n vanish. Given joint minor circuits of size H and depth e, Q has size O(H+m⁴+m²n+1), depth<=e+8 over binary constants without determinant primitives. At m2n,i=n,j=n+1, setting B's listed n columns to the identity restricts Cij to the generic n-square determinant; individual minor registers have no polynomial-size uniformly fixed-depth binary arithmetic circuits. Each weight Gij=Di Wij Cij is nevertheless Boolean-zero even for arbitrary Boolean E: Wij either vanishes or forces the minor's column i zero. Hence hard unmasked minors do not imply full Q hardness. Column-i Laplace gives Gij=Di sum_r>i W_(ij,ri)(Eri²+Eri) Cij^(r), reducing order by one but retaining growing principal blocks when r=j. No polynomial-size fixed-depth combined correction or all-certificate bound follows.

Explicit intermediate restriction and mask controls supply no efficient fixed-depth full implementation or all-certificate bound.
